summary: mcp__github__search_issues returns total_count 0 for every query on a private repo while gh search returns results — a silent wrong-answer, not an error
description: On cbartens/bkit (PRIVATE), mcp__github__search_issues returns {total_count:0} for every query including the control `repo:cbartens/bkit is:issue is:open`, despite 39 matching issues. `gh search issues --repo cbartens/bkit worktree` and `gh api search/issues` (total_count 39) both succeed with the same account. Impact: bkit-design Step 3.1 (related-issues search) specifies this MCP tool and its own rule says `0 hits -> None.`, so the workflow records `None.` and proceeds — silently dropping related-issue context from every design on a private repo. Failure is silent (clean 0, no error), so the `on call error -> Search unavailable.` branch never fires.
rootCause: Not yet root-caused. Candidates: GitHub search API requires different token scope/visibility handling for PRIVATE repos than the REST issue endpoints the MCP server uses elsewhere (issue_read/list_issues work fine); or the MCP server drops the owner/repo scoping params. Note gh (keyring classic token) succeeds where the MCP server (GH_TOKEN fine-grained PAT) returns 0 — consistent with the known GH_TOKEN scope gap.
remediation: Two parts. (1) bkit workflow: Step 3.1 must not treat 0 hits as authoritative — distinguish `search unavailable` from `genuinely no hits` (e.g. probe with a control query, or require the mapped gh fallback per #341 6b/6c). (2) #341 design input: this is direct evidence that 6i (trackers stay on MCP) has a SILENT-failure hole — the gh->MCP fallback rule (6b) covers gh-outage but nothing covers MCP-returns-garbage. The design should add a rule that MCP tracker reads which can silently return empty are either verified or mapped to a gh fallback.

summary: bkit-status-fold.test.ts hashed via macOS-only `md5`, passing locally but failing on Linux CI
description: Sub-plan 1's T1.3 test .bkit/src/bkit-status-fold.test.ts:68 computed the BKIT_STATUS_FOLD blob md5 by shelling out to `sh -c '...' | md5`. `md5` is the BSD/macOS binary; Linux (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest) ships `md5sum` instead, so the pipe errored 'Command failed'. The test passed on the macOS dev box across every local `pnpm test` run this build and only surfaced when CI ran the workflow_dispatch lane (run 29486640718, bkit-tests-unit). Local-only green is exactly the class docs/testing.md and feedback_verify_install_and_upgrade_live warn about. All other lanes (integration, static) passed; bkit-tests-check failed only as a downstream consequence of the unit lane.
rootCause: Portability: shell-out to a BSD-only command (`md5`) with no Linux fallback, in a test that only ever ran on macOS locally before CI.
remediation: Hash in-process with node:crypto createHash('md5').update(out).digest('hex') — platform-independent, no shell-out. Verified all three (Node crypto, macOS md5, MEASURED_MD5) agree at ed1c4a236d35499f39033206d5b75480. Fixed on feat/58-workflow-counters before merge.

summary: poll_dispatch() sets GH_ALL_ERRORED=false inside a command-substitution subshell — the assignment never reaches the caller, so GH_ALL_ERRORED stays 'true' even when gh succeeded
description: The pre-#341 inline CI-Dispatch Gate kernel (bkit-build.md close-workflow, bkit-debug.md PR-mode + LOCAL-mode) calls its poll function as `R=$(poll_dispatch)` to capture the echoed found/none/err result. `$(...)` forks a subshell, so poll_dispatch's own `GH_ALL_ERRORED="false"` assignment (made on a successful gh call) is scoped to that subshell and discarded on return — the caller's GH_ALL_ERRORED never flips from its initial 'true'. Downstream, `if [ "$GH_ALL_ERRORED" = "true" ]` (the post-kernel unresolved(gh-error) branch) can misclassify a run where gh worked fine but genuinely found no CI check as gh-error instead of no-ci/timeout-dirty/autoroute-mismatch. Discovered while extracting this logic into bkit_wait_ci (tests/bkit-runtime.bats row 5) — a bats assertion on ALLERR=false after a successful zero-result poll failed until fixed.
rootCause: Command-substitution subshell scoping: variable writes inside $(fn) never propagate to the parent shell.
remediation: Fixed in the #341 extraction: bkit_wait_ci (.bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/bkit-runtime.sh) derives CI_WAIT_ALL_ERRORED from the poll's echoed result ([ "$_bwc_r" != "err" ] && CI_WAIT_ALL_ERRORED="false") in the CALLING shell, after the substitution returns, instead of inside the subshelled poll function. The inline poll_dispatch()/GH_ALL_ERRORED duplicates in bkit-build.md/bkit-debug.md are being replaced by calls to the fixed bkit_wait_ci in the same change.

summary: bkit-ship.md and bkit-auto.md fixes from the first #363 challenge-remediation pass never reached the .claude/.cursor/.opencode mirrors that a cloud dispatch actually executes
description: After build-challenge-remediate attempt 1 landed the CI_DEV FID slug allowlist (.bkit/workflows/bkit-auto.md:103-105) and the (subsequently found insufficient) marker handoff (.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md:255-262,686-704), none of .claude/commands/{bkit-ship,bkit-auto}.md, .cursor/commands/{...}.md, .opencode/commands/{...}.md were regenerated. summary: A friction row landed on dev with a literal $(date +%s)000 as its ts, making the line invalid JSON and the ledger unfoldable
description: `.bkit/friction.jsonl` line 26 (key 384-bats-pre-push-test-isolation) was written as {"id":…,"ts":$(date +%s)000,…}: the command substitution never expanded, so the value is a bare literal and jq fails the whole file with Invalid numeric literal. The row also used "id" instead of the schema key "key" and omitted kind/repo/bkitVersion/workflow/step/category/severity. Present on origin/dev, so every reader of that ledger — bkit harvest, any fold, the analysis pass — has been failing or silently skipping since it landed.
rootCause: the row was appended from a context where the substitution was not evaluated (single-quoted heredoc or a literal-quoted argument) and nothing validated the line afterwards. Appends are best-effort and exit 0 by design, so an unparseable row raises no signal at write time.
remediation: repaired in place: ts set to the introducing commit date (1785295536000), id renamed to key, missing envelope and per-kind fields filled. Durable fix is a parse check on append — pipe the row through jq -c before >> so a malformed line can never land, and add a ledger-validity assertion to the test suite.

summary: ship-deferred-sweep.md was created inside the feature worktree per Step 5's literal cd instruction, but no step commits it before the worktree is removed in Step 12, so it is silently destroyed
description: bkit-ship.md Step 5 instructs the @bkit-ship-deferred-sweep subagent to cd into {WORKTREE_PATH} and Create docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ship-deferred-sweep.md there. Unlike Step 4's B2 conflict-resolve path (which explicitly commits+force-pushes its artifact to feat/{FID}), Step 5 has no commit step of its own, and Step 6 immediately squash-merges the PR without picking up worktree-only files. Step 12 (Worktree Cleanup) then force-removes the worktree. The artifact — the pre-merge completeness gate's own evidence file — is lost before it ever lands in a commit, on either the feat branch or BOOK_ROOT (the main dev tree), even though its verdict (PASS/FAIL) is correctly recorded in status.jsonl and gates the merge. Only the subagent's chat-return summary survives, not the full markdown artifact.
rootCause: BOOK_ROOT (main tree) vs WORKTREE_PATH (feature worktree) are two different physical directories when RUNTIME_WORKTREES=true. Step 5's cd instruction targets WORKTREE_PATH for consistency with Steps 2-4's convention of operating on the feature branch, but docs/plans/**/logs/{FID}/ artifacts are bookkeeping (per the Step 2 comment 'bookkeeping never rides the branch') and should be written directly under BOOK_ROOT like Step 1's ship-input.md and Step 10's ship-summary.md/ship-update-docs.md are.
remediation: Either (a) have Step 5 instruct the subagent to cd into BOOK_ROOT instead of WORKTREE_PATH for artifact creation (matching Steps 1/10's convention), or (b) add an explicit copy-to-BOOK_ROOT / commit step after Step 5 creates the artifact, before Step 6 merges. Also audit Step 2's ship-worktree-setup / ship-regression-guard artifacts for the same class of gap.

summary: bkit-cloud-ctx-step.integration.test.ts T13/H1 began failing on 2026-08-01 with no code change, because its helpers pinned the docs/plans/202607 bucket
description: readStatusRows() and the truncated-directory assertion both hardcoded docs/plans/202607/logs/. The ctx step's dispatch-cap guard resolves its status dir by DISCOVERING an existing bucket (find docs/plans/*/logs/$guard_fid | sort | head -1) and falling back to docs/plans/$(date -u +%Y%m)/logs/$guard_fid/ when the FID has no logs yet. Tests that pre-seed rows via seedDevDispatchRows() create 202607 first, so discovery finds it and they keep passing. T13/H1 seeds nothing, so the guard took the fallback and wrote the dev-dispatch row to the CURRENT month. The assertion read 202607, got an empty array, and failed. The test therefore passed for every run in July 2026 and failed every run from 2026-08-01 onward.
rootCause: the fixture encoded 'the current month' as a literal at authoring time. Nothing in the suite ties the expected bucket to the same clock the code under test reads, so the assertion silently changed meaning at the month rollover rather than failing loudly when authored.
remediation: replaced the pinned path with a statusDirs() helper that enumerates every docs/plans/*/logs/<fid>/ present, mirroring the step's own discovery; readStatusRows() aggregates across buckets and the truncated-id assertion now asserts absence in ALL buckets. Durable rule: a test asserting a date-derived path must derive it from the same clock as the code, never from a literal.

summary: Same 5s-timeout flake now also observed in bkit-cloud-ctx-step.integration.test.ts T17 under parallel vitest run
description: Third file confirmed in the same class on 2026-08-23: bkit-cloud-ctx-step.integration.test.ts T17 ("a counter write that cannot land on origin/dev fails closed") failed with Error: Test timed out in 5000ms during a full parallel `pnpm test`, and passed 20/20 when the file was run alone, on the same tree. Consecutive full runs reddened a different subset each time (2 failures, then 1) with no edit between them. It spawns real git push / bash subprocesses against a temp origin, so it shares the root cause already recorded here for bkit-upgrade.integration.test.ts and bkit-check-opencode.integration.test.ts. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` passes all 95 files / 3487 tests.
rootCause: no testTimeout is configured and no integration test sets one explicitly, so tests whose body is a multi-second child process share the unit-test budget. Load from any other concurrently-running worker pushes them over it.
remediation: Unchanged: give every subprocess-spawning integration file a timeout matched to its real cost (per-file testTimeout, or a vitest project override scoped to *.integration.test.ts), keeping the 5s default for unit tests. Until then --no-file-parallelism is the trustworthy invocation. Scope now covers three files, so the fix belongs in vitest.config.ts rather than file-by-file.

summary: Subprocess-spawning integration tests intermittently time out at the 5000ms default under high machine load
description: Two full pnpm test runs during #380 build returned 22 and 14 failures respectively, ALL of them Error: Test timed out in 5000ms with zero assertion failures, at load average 62.9/43.8. summary: The #380 dev-lock roadmap mirror in build/debug checked out and pushed dev in the main checkout with no adopt-mode fence
description: Introduced by this PR (aa3e45ed, sub-plan 1 Task 7) — NOT pre-existing; the block is absent from dev. The dev-side mirror runs git -C "$REPO_ROOT" checkout dev / commit / push origin dev to mirror the roadmap ledger line onto dev, guarded only by the dev lock. In adopt mode (RUNTIME_WORKTREES=false, WORKTREE_PATH == REPO_ROOT) $REPO_ROOT IS the session sole working tree, so the checkout swaps the branch out from under the in-progress build/debug run, over a tree still holding uncommitted feature work. CUR_BRANCH is restored afterwards so blast radius is bounded, but the fence that exists precisely to refuse this (bkit_close_guard_checkout, which requires RUNTIME_WORKTREES=true AND RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true) was never consulted. Flagged by build-plan-verify-holistic as an untraced risk and carried through the ship deferred sweep without a trace being owed.
rootCause: The close-hook block was written without the runtime double-guard, and the obvious guard could not be dropped in verbatim: bkit_close_guard_checkout installs an EXIT trap, and bash traps REPLACE rather than chain, so it would clobber the DEVLOCK-removal trap and leak the dev lock. Compounding it, RUNTIME_WORKTREES/RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES are set by bkit_runtime_detect in an EARLIER, SEPARATE fenced shell invocation and are not in scope in the close block — so the naive fix (testing those vars inline) would have compared against unset and silently disabled the mirror entirely.
remediation: Added an inline fence at the top of the mirror subshell in both bkit-build.md and bkit-debug.md, before the dev lock is even acquired: if [ "$WT" = "$REPO_ROOT" ] then log and exit 0. Derived from local facts already assigned in the same fenced block rather than out-of-scope RUNTIME_* vars. Faithful proxy for the double guard because the runtime capability table moves both flags together (LOCAL/GITHUB_ACTION/CLOUD_CURSOR => worktrees=true+devpushes=true; CLOUD_CLAUDE/UNKNOWN => both false). Behaviour verified by executing the fence for both modes: adopt skips, mint proceeds. Host mirrors regenerated; bkit check 0 writes.

summary: The fold additive-only dedup compared tracker and ledger keys across two namespaces, so every ledger-backed FID also rendered a duplicate tracker row
description: Found by testing the enrichment path before enabling it at ship. The fold treats tracker rows as ADDITIVE ONLY — a tracker row is kept only when its FID has no ledger row — via map(select(.key as $k | ($known | index($k)) == null)). But the two sides are keyed in DIFFERENT namespaces: ledger keys are FIDs ({ISSUE_ID}-{slug}, e.g. 412-export-csv or TEAM-42-delta) while the enrichment step maps tracker rows to the raw issue id (key: "#{number}", e.g. #412). A raw string compare never matched, so the additive-only guard never fired for ANY enriched FID. Reproduced: a ledger holding 412-export-csv plus a tracker row #412 rendered BOTH in the Build section — the same issue listed twice under two different keys. Every wired-tracker consumer has been seeing this on every design/plan/build/debug close since the enrichment landed; it was not caught because bkit dogfoods with githubProject false and a ledger migrated from completed.md, whose synthesised keys never collide either way. Distinct from the OPEN deferral 380-bootstrap-seed-key-namespace-mismatch-vs-migrated-completed-md-keys, which is about bootstrap-seed FIDs vs migrated completed.md keys.
rootCause: Two key namespaces (ledger FID vs tracker issue id) compared raw, with no normalisation step between them.
remediation: Added a tid normaliser to BKIT_ROADMAP_FOLD that maps both sides to one tracker identity before the additive-only test: strip a leading #, lowercase, then take the leading numeric segment (github) or the leading alpha-numeric pair (linear), mirroring the ship reverse-sync FID convention (^[0-9]+ / ^[A-Za-z]+-[0-9]+). Keys matching neither shape — notably migrated completed-<slug>-<hash> rows — pass through unchanged so they can never falsely collapse. Verified on four fixtures: github dup suppressed while a genuine tracker-only row is kept, linear dup suppressed, legacy keys not collapsed, empty tracker unaffected. Both fold copies kept byte-identical.

summary: No phase workflow (design/plan/build/debug/ship) ever calls bkit_runtime_row — the durable GH_OK carrier the gh->MCP fallback rule (T14) and D25 cross-check depend on is never written to status.jsonl
description: D21/Flow-1 (design doc) states GH_OK is probed once at Step 1 and later blocks read it back from the runtime-resolved status.jsonl row instead of re-probing gh (docs/observability.md and .bkit/workflows.md already document this as the intended mechanism, per Sub-Plan 1 T3). In the actually-shipped workflow prose, bkit_runtime_detect/bkit_runtime_assert_resolved are called at Step 2 (Worktree Setup) of each of the five phase workflows, but bkit_runtime_row (the function that prints the runtime-resolved row) is never called anywhere in .bkit/workflows/*.md -- grep confirms zero call sites. Consequence: (1) any block after Step 2 that needs GH_OK per D21 has no durable source to read it from; (2) bkit_close_guard_cross_check (D25) reads the LATEST runtime-resolved row via jq, finds none, and its null-check falls through to ghOk="unknown" -- the cross-check's GH_OK=false branch can never fire, so D25 is currently vacuous in every real run even though its bats tests (synthetic status.jsonl) pass.
rootCause: No sub-plan task (T3/T6/T7/T8/T9) explicitly named wiring bkit_runtime_row into Step 1 of the five phase workflows as a Done-when criterion; the shim function and its bats coverage were built (T3), and downstream consumers (T9 D25, T14 fallback rule) were written assuming the row already exists per the design doc, but the actual Step-1 emission call site was never added by any task.
remediation: Add a bkit_runtime_detect + bkit_runtime_assert_resolved + bkit_runtime_row(workflow, at) >> status.jsonl call to Step 1 of design/plan/build/debug/ship, after FID is finalised (the point most Step-1 blocks already resolve). Expected to surface concretely at Sub-Plan 6/T16's live mode-3 run (WS-16 is the only guarantee that consumption honours the flags, per the design's own accepted limit) -- fix there or as a fast-follow once confirmed.

summary: bkit [auto route] squash-subject marker is never threaded onto dev in a cloud dispatch — the #363 post-merge dev trigger feature is functionally inert
description: bkit-ship.md Step 5 (.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md:686-704) reads AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX back from a BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE handoff written at Step 1 (:255-262) via `echo "BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE=$BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`. In a claude-code-action/opencode cloud dispatch every agent Bash tool call executes inside one Action step, so $GITHUB_ENV (which only propagates BETWEEN separate Action steps) never carries the value forward; Step 5 falls back to the dead `echo "${LABELS:-}" | grep -q 'bkit:auto'` read (LABELS unset in that shell), so AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX is always empty. bkit-cloud.yml's free-tier gate (contains(head_commit.message, 'bkit [auto route]')) can therefore never match a dev push, and no dev-CI-failure /bkit-debug dispatch can ever occur — the load-bearing mechanism #363 exists to ship.
rootCause: GitHub Actions $GITHUB_ENV is applied by the runner only between separate workflow steps; it does not propagate across separate Bash tool calls an agent makes within one claude-code-action/opencode run step. A file-path handoff written this way is silently invisible at the point of use in a cloud dispatch.
remediation: Re-derive AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX inside the SAME bash fence at Step 5 with a call that depends on no prior shell state (e.g. gh issue view {ISSUE_ID} --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qxF 'bkit:auto'), per docs/knowledge.jsonl key 363-workflow-md-shell-var-does-not-survive-bash-tool-call-boundary idiom (1); delete the $GITHUB_ENV handoff entirely.

summary: bkit-upgrade and bkit-check-opencode integration tests fail a varying subset on every parallel `vitest run` and pass in isolation, because subprocess installs run on vitest's default 5s timeout
description: Each full parallel run reds a DIFFERENT subset of .bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.integration.test.ts and .bkit/src/bkit-check-opencode.integration.test.ts (observed 2, 3, 4 and 6 failures across consecutive runs on an unchanged tree); the same files pass 20/20 when run alone, and `vitest run --no-file-parallelism` passes the whole suite. The failure is always `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`, never an assertion. These tests spawn real `bkit install` / `bkit upgrade` / `bkit check` subprocesses against a temp consumer dir, each taking seconds; vitest.config.ts sets no testTimeout, so they inherit the 5000ms default and only pass when the machine is otherwise idle. Effect: the suite is not trustworthy under parallelism, and a real regression in these files is indistinguishable from the noise.
rootCause: no testTimeout is configured and no integration test sets one explicitly, so tests whose body is a multi-second child process share the unit-test budget. Load from any other concurrently-running worker pushes them over it.
remediation: give the subprocess-spawning integration files a timeout matched to their real cost rather than the unit default — either a per-file testTimeout or a vitest project override scoped to `*.integration.test.ts`, keeping the 5s default for unit tests so a genuinely hung one still fails fast. Until then `vitest run --no-file-parallelism` is the trustworthy invocation.

summary: maskNonExpansions blanks an arbitrary multi-line span whenever a fenced-block comment contains an apostrophe, because it masks '...' with no awareness of leading # comments
description: bkit-block-locality-audit.test.ts:254's maskNonExpansions runs out.replace(/'[^']*'/g, blank) over a fenced workflow block with no comment-awareness. A single possessive apostrophe inside a `#` comment (e.g. "script's") pairs with the next literal single-quote anywhere later in the block and blanks every line in between, including real VAR= assignments — the audit then reports a bogus unassigned-$VAR failure pointing at the wrong line. Hit during the #380 round-2 ship remediation (commit 8427ed08): a possessive in a workflow fenced-block comment swallowed a real TRACKER_ROWS= assignment several lines down; worked around by rewording the comment. The defect itself is untouched and will recur for the next author who writes a possessive in any workflow fenced-block comment.
rootCause: Regex-based quote masking (/'[^']*'/g) has no notion of a leading # comment token, so an apostrophe inside a comment is treated as a real quote-open and pairs with an unrelated later quote.
remediation: Not yet fixed — out of #380's scope. Candidate: strip # comment-to-end-of-line spans before running the quote-mask regex, or make the mask comment-aware (skip matches whose opening quote is preceded by an unescaped # earlier on the same line with no closing quote before it).

summary: tests/ship-failure-path.bats's awk block selector matches the bare substring bkit-book-commit.sh, so a comment mention counts as an invocation
description: tests/ship-failure-path.bats:184's awk block selector selects any fenced block containing the substring bkit-book-commit.sh, with no distinction between an actual invocation and a comment merely naming the file. That inflates the exactly-3-wired-blocks assertion at :192 and the every-invocation-is-guarded assertion at :201 whenever a comment mentions the filename. Hit during the #380 round-2 ship remediation (commit 2b669577): a comment naming bkit-book-commit.sh broke both assertions; worked around by removing the filename from the comment. The selector itself is unfixed and will recur for the next author who mentions the script by name in a comment near a fenced block.
rootCause: The awk selector matches on a bare substring rather than a real invocation pattern (e.g. a call site with `.` or `bash` prefix, or a comment-stripped scan).
remediation: Not yet fixed — out of #380's scope. Candidate: tighten the awk selector to match only real invocation shapes (e.g. leading whitespace + optional `.`/`bash` + the script path, not preceded by `#`), or strip comment lines before the substring scan.

summary: telemetry-failopen.bats ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE read-only-dir case cannot fail when the suite runs as root
description: tests/telemetry-failopen.bats:159-171 creates a directory, chmod 555 it, and asserts the jq append emits the [bkit-roadmap] fail-open line. Under uid 0 the mode bits do not deny the write, the append succeeds, OUTPUT is empty and the [[ "$OUTPUT" == *"[bkit-roadmap]"* ]] assertion at line 169 fails. Observed at 58dc0550: 234 of 235 bats cases ok, case 233 not ok. The fail-open behaviour under test is correct; only the test setup is unreachable as root.
rootCause: the case models unwritability with directory permission bits alone, which uid 0 bypasses; no uid guard and no alternative unwritable-target strategy
remediation: gate the case on a non-zero uid (skip with a reason when id -u is 0), or make the target genuinely unwritable regardless of uid (append to a path under a directory component that is a regular file, or to an immutable/EROFS mount) so the fail-open branch is exercised on every host

summary: detectBkitNotOnPath advisory test fails inside a remote Claude Code / Cursor agent session
description: The case at .bkit/src/bkit-preflight.test.ts:1780 sets PATH to a nonexistent directory and deletes process.env.CI, then expects detectBkitNotOnPath() to return a finding. detectBkitNotOnPath (.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts:1309) short-circuits on isCloudOrCi(), which also reads CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE and CURSOR_REMOTE_AGENT. Any run inside a remote Claude Code or Cursor agent session has CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true in the environment, so the function returns null and the assertion fails. Reproduced at 58dc0550: 3728 passed, 1 failed, the failure being this case. Pre-existing on origin/dev (87b21dc9) — neither the function nor the case is touched by the #380 branch.
rootCause: the test neutralises only one of the three env vars isCloudOrCi() consults; CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE and CURSOR_REMOTE_AGENT leak in from the host agent session
remediation: delete CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE and CURSOR_REMOTE_AGENT alongside CI in that case (and in the sibling null-expecting case), restoring them in the existing afterEach env restore

summary: Test env isolation did not clear the cloud-agent env vars that isCloudOrCi reads
description: Fixed. The describe block now snapshots and restores the full env (matching the detectDirenvMissing block in the same file), and both non-hermetic cases delete CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE and CURSOR_REMOTE_AGENT alongside CI. Verified green with CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true set, the exact environment that reproduced the failure.

summary: chmod 555 precondition cannot fail under uid 0, so the fail-open branch went unexercised
description: Fixed. Three sibling cases in tests/telemetry-failopen.bats built their unwritable target with mkdir + chmod 555, which uid 0 bypasses; all three passed vacuously off-root and failed under root. Suite is now 235/235 under root.
rootCause: chmod-based permission blocks are advisory for uid 0; the redirect succeeded, so the || echo fail-open branch never ran and the [bkit-roadmap] / [bkit-telemetry] assertion failed.
remediation: Target path now sits under a regular-file path component, so the append fails with ENOTDIR for every uid. Applied to all three cases (stats.jsonl best-effort, docs/roadmap.jsonl, ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE); the paired chmod 755 restores dropped.

summary: staging-failure case used chmod 0555 on .git, which uid 0 bypasses
description: Fixed. tests/book-commit.bats:154 blocked staging with chmod 0555 on the test repos .git; under root the commit succeeded, so the assertion that the script exits non-zero failed. Same root-bypass defect class as the telemetry-failopen cases, in a second file; pre-existing on dev and unrelated to #380.
rootCause: chmod is advisory for uid 0, so git add/commit still wrote to .git and the script took its success path.
remediation: Precondition is now a pre-existing .git/index.lock, which git refuses to take for every uid; lock removed after the run.

summary: bkit telemetry validate checks alias collisions and sequential keys only; the ts-mint and append-once invariants go unenforced
description: Observed across the five docs ledgers: 76 rows carry a whole-second ts (ts % 1000 == 0), which .bkit/jsonl.md § Write Idiom states is rejected, and one carries ts:0; 36 byte-identical duplicate lines exist (same ts, key and status — true double-appends, not same-key state updates). .bkit/stats.jsonl is clean, so the shell append idiom is sound and the drift is confined to model-written rows. bkit telemetry validate scans all of them and reports OK.
rootCause: validate implements only the DE-/KN- alias-collision and sequential-key rules; it has no ts-shape check and no exact-duplicate-line check, so a hand-typed or copied ts and a re-run append both pass silently.
remediation: Add two rules to bkit telemetry validate: WARN on ts % 1000 == 0 or ts <= 0, and WARN on byte-identical duplicate lines within a ledger. Existing rows cannot be repaired — the ledgers are append-only and prior lines are never edited — so the rules gate new rows only.

summary: Shipped section ranks by ledger append time, so a historic backfill outranks genuinely recent ships
description: bkit-roadmap-fold.sh renders the Shipped section as `sort_by(-.ts) | .[0:10]`, but `ts` is the ledger APPEND time, not the date the feature shipped, and .bkit/jsonl.md forbids a literal ts (it must be minted by jq at append time, and whole-second values are rejected). So any backfill of historic SHIPPED rows sorts as the most recent ships. Observed after a 22-row migration backfill: the Shipped table showed ten 2026-05-era features and evicted 380-roadmap-analysis-refresh and 363-widen-bkit-cloud-trigger, which had actually shipped that same week. Self-corrects only after ten further real ships.
remediation: Give the feature row an explicit ship-date field (e.g. shippedAt, free to be a historic literal since it is not the ledger identity) and sort the Shipped section on that, falling back to ts when absent. Alternative: order the Shipped section by the tracker close date where an issue is wired.

summary: bkit-ship.md and bkit-auto.md fixes from the first #363 challenge-remediation pass never reached the .claude/.cursor/.opencode mirrors that a cloud dispatch actually executes
description: After build-challenge-remediate attempt 1 landed the CI_DEV FID slug allowlist (.bkit/workflows/bkit-auto.md:103-105) and the (subsequently found insufficient) marker handoff (.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md:255-262,686-704), none of .claude/commands/{bkit-ship,bkit-auto}.md, .cursor/commands/{...}.md, .opencode/commands/{...}.md were regenerated. summary: ship-deferred-sweep.md was created inside the feature worktree per Step 5's literal cd instruction, but no step commits it before the worktree is removed in Step 12, so it is silently destroyed
description: bkit-ship.md Step 5 instructs the @bkit-ship-deferred-sweep subagent to cd into {WORKTREE_PATH} and Create docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ship-deferred-sweep.md there. Unlike Step 4's B2 conflict-resolve path (which explicitly commits+force-pushes its artifact to feat/{FID}), Step 5 has no commit step of its own, and Step 6 immediately squash-merges the PR without picking up worktree-only files. Step 12 (Worktree Cleanup) then force-removes the worktree. The artifact — the pre-merge completeness gate's own evidence file — is lost before it ever lands in a commit, on either the feat branch or BOOK_ROOT (the main dev tree), even though its verdict (PASS/FAIL) is correctly recorded in status.jsonl and gates the merge. Only the subagent's chat-return summary survives, not the full markdown artifact.
rootCause: BOOK_ROOT (main tree) vs WORKTREE_PATH (feature worktree) are two different physical directories when RUNTIME_WORKTREES=true. Step 5's cd instruction targets WORKTREE_PATH for consistency with Steps 2-4's convention of operating on the feature branch, but docs/plans/**/logs/{FID}/ artifacts are bookkeeping (per the Step 2 comment 'bookkeeping never rides the branch') and should be written directly under BOOK_ROOT like Step 1's ship-input.md and Step 10's ship-summary.md/ship-update-docs.md are.
remediation: Either (a) have Step 5 instruct the subagent to cd into BOOK_ROOT instead of WORKTREE_PATH for artifact creation (matching Steps 1/10's convention), or (b) add an explicit copy-to-BOOK_ROOT / commit step after Step 5 creates the artifact, before Step 6 merges. Also audit Step 2's ship-worktree-setup / ship-regression-guard artifacts for the same class of gap.

summary: mcp__github__search_issues returns total_count 0 for every query on a private repo while gh search returns results — a silent wrong-answer, not an error
description: On cbartens/bkit (PRIVATE), mcp__github__search_issues returns {total_count:0} for every query including the control `repo:cbartens/bkit is:issue is:open`, despite 39 matching issues. `gh search issues --repo cbartens/bkit worktree` and `gh api search/issues` (total_count 39) both succeed with the same account. Impact: bkit-design Step 3.1 (related-issues search) specifies this MCP tool and its own rule says `0 hits -> None.`, so the workflow records `None.` and proceeds — silently dropping related-issue context from every design on a private repo. Failure is silent (clean 0, no error), so the `on call error -> Search unavailable.` branch never fires.
rootCause: Not yet root-caused. Candidates: GitHub search API requires different token scope/visibility handling for PRIVATE repos than the REST issue endpoints the MCP server uses elsewhere (issue_read/list_issues work fine); or the MCP server drops the owner/repo scoping params. Note gh (keyring classic token) succeeds where the MCP server (GH_TOKEN fine-grained PAT) returns 0 — consistent with the known GH_TOKEN scope gap.
remediation: Two parts. (1) bkit workflow: Step 3.1 must not treat 0 hits as authoritative — distinguish `search unavailable` from `genuinely no hits` (e.g. probe with a control query, or require the mapped gh fallback per #341 6b/6c). (2) #341 design input: this is direct evidence that 6i (trackers stay on MCP) has a SILENT-failure hole — the gh->MCP fallback rule (6b) covers gh-outage but nothing covers MCP-returns-garbage. The design should add a rule that MCP tracker reads which can silently return empty are either verified or mapped to a gh fallback.

summary: bkit-ship.md never writes a workflow-started row, so every ship run on an FID folds into one run
description: Build, plan, design and debug each append {type:"workflow-started"} to status.jsonl at start; ship does not (0 occurrences in .bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md). The fold (bkit-status-fold.sh) starts a new run only on workflow-started, so all ship invocations on one FID collapse into a single run. Effects: (1) counter_next/counter_current are active-run scoped, so MERGE_ATTEMPT carries over between separate ship runs — on 380-roadmap-analysis-refresh (4 ship runs, 3 failed) a new ship run would start at MERGE_ATTEMPT 2 of MAX_MERGE_ATTEMPT 3; (2) bkit-ship.md:1399 SHIP_START is always empty, so the outcome row records durationSeconds 0 and frictionAdded/deferralsAdded/failuresAdded count every ship row since epoch instead of this run; (3) bkit-ship.md:1377 COUNTER_VALUE counts workflow-started rows and is always 0.
rootCause: The workflow-started emit (and its resume re-emit) was removed from bkit-ship.md in 80660ac0 (#384, PR #395) restructure; the #384 plan does not mention removing it.
remediation: Restore the workflow-started append in ship Step 1 (same shape as bkit-build.md:358) and add a ship-invariants test asserting all five workflows emit it.

summary: On a cloud runtime, a ship Failure Path entered AFTER the merge (red squash-merge CI, Switch to Dev or cleanup error) commits FAILED bookkeeping to the current branch and pushes it, but the feature branch was deleted by the merge and dev is not pushable there
description: bkit-ship.md Failure Path step 7 pushes TARGET=$(git branch --show-current) when RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES != true. Post-merge, gh pr merge --delete-branch has removed the remote feature branch and may have switched the checkout to dev; the push either recreates an orphan feature branch or is refused on dev. The ship-merge-ci row Close Workflow writes before routing a red merge to the Failure Path is in that flush. Not live-verified on a cloud run.
rootCause: The Failure Path flush predates the post-merge close publish path (close worktree off origin/dev, push dev, else ship-close/{FID} PR) and still targets the current branch.
remediation: When FAILED_STATE = MERGED and RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES != true, publish the FAILED flush through the same close-worktree + dev push / ship-close PR path Close Workflow uses.

summary: bkit harvest rewrote harvest/ to one fold winner per key, so a row an earlier run had pruned from the consumer could be dropped from the store and exist nowhere
description: Found by the #343 audit (docs/audits/202610/harvest.md, harvest-1 + harvest-2). Run 2 over app-gether-life dropped 8 friction rows run 1 had already pruned; they survived only in the consumer git HEAD. Two causes: (1) fold() sorted with a.ts - b.ts, and 22 legacy consumer rows carry an ISO-string or missing ts, so the comparator returned NaN, the sort was void, and the winner per key depended on file order, which differed between runs; (2) runHarvest rewrote each store file from fold(), keeping only winners, so a winner flip or a newer same-key row evicted rows the store was the only copy of.
rootCause: The store was written from a lossy projection (fold by identity) of the rows it was banking, and the fold ordering was not total over legacy ts values.
remediation: Store keeps every distinct row, deduped by content only, never rewritten from fold; readers fold. fold() and the telemetry sorts use compareTs, which parses ISO-string ts and sorts missing ts oldest. Regression tests in bkit-harvest.integration.test.ts and bkit-telemetry.test.ts.

summary: maskNonExpansions blanks an arbitrary multi-line span whenever a fenced-block comment contains an apostrophe, because it masks '...' with no awareness of leading # comments
description: .bkit/src/bkit-block-locality-audit.test.ts:260's maskNonExpansions runs out.replace(/'[^']*'/g, blank) over a fenced workflow block with no comment-awareness. A single possessive apostrophe inside a `#` comment (e.g. "script's") pairs with the next literal single-quote anywhere later in the block and blanks every line in between, including real VAR= assignments — the audit then reports a bogus unassigned-$VAR failure pointing at the wrong line. Hit during the #380 round-2 ship remediation (commit 8427ed08): a possessive in a workflow fenced-block comment swallowed a real TRACKER_ROWS= assignment several lines down; worked around by rewording the comment. The defect itself is untouched and will recur for the next author who writes a possessive in any workflow fenced-block comment.
rootCause: Regex-based quote masking (/'[^']*'/g) has no notion of a leading # comment token, so an apostrophe inside a comment is treated as a real quote-open and pairs with an unrelated later quote.
remediation: Not yet fixed — out of #380's scope. Candidate: strip # comment-to-end-of-line spans before running the quote-mask regex, or make the mask comment-aware (skip matches whose opening quote is preceded by an unescaped # earlier on the same line with no closing quote before it).

summary: bkit telemetry validate checks alias collisions and sequential keys only; the ts-mint and append-once invariants go unenforced
description: Observed across the five docs ledgers: 76 rows carry a whole-second ts (ts % 1000 == 0), which .bkit/jsonl.md § Write Idiom states is rejected, and one carries ts:0; 36 byte-identical duplicate lines exist (same ts, key and status — true double-appends, not same-key state updates). .bkit/stats.jsonl is clean, so the shell append idiom is sound and the drift is confined to model-written rows. bkit telemetry validate scans all of them and reports OK.
rootCause: validate implements only the DE-/KN- alias-collision and sequential-key rules; it has no ts-shape check and no exact-duplicate-line check, so a hand-typed or copied ts and a re-run append both pass silently.
remediation: Add two rules to bkit telemetry validate: WARN on ts % 1000 == 0 or ts <= 0, and WARN on byte-identical duplicate lines within a ledger. Existing rows cannot be repaired — the ledgers are append-only and prior lines are never edited — so the rules gate new rows only.

summary: On a cloud runtime, a ship Failure Path entered AFTER the merge (red squash-merge CI, Switch to Dev or cleanup error) commits FAILED bookkeeping to the current branch and pushes it, but the feature branch was deleted by the merge and dev is not pushable there
description: bkit-ship.md Failure Path step 7 pushes TARGET=$(git branch --show-current) when RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES != true. remediation: When FAILED_STATE = MERGED and RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES != true, publish the FAILED flush through the same close-worktree + dev push / ship-close PR path Close Workflow uses.

rootCause: Per-project convention edits .bkit/workflows/*.md by hand and defers mirror regeneration (.claude/.cursor/.opencode) to bkit install/bkit upgrade at session end, but the build-challenge-remediate pass ended the session without running it, so the fix never reached the artifacts claude-code-action/opencode run actually execute.

summary: ship-deferred-sweep.md was created inside the feature worktree per Step 5's literal cd instruction, but no step commits it before the worktree is removed in Step 12, so it is silently destroyed
description: bkit-ship.md Step 5 instructs the @bkit-ship-deferred-sweep subagent to cd into {WORKTREE_PATH} and Create docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ship-deferred-sweep.md there. Unlike Step 4's B2 conflict-resolve path (which explicitly commits+force-pushes its artifact to feat/{FID}), Step 5 has no commit step of its own, and Step 6 immediately squash-merges the PR without picking up worktree-only files. Step 12 (Worktree Cleanup) then force-removes the worktree. The artifact — the pre-merge completeness gate's own evidence file — is lost before it ever lands in a commit, on either the feat branch or BOOK_ROOT (the main dev tree), even though its verdict (PASS/FAIL) is correctly recorded in status.jsonl and gates the merge. Only the subagent's chat-return summary survives, not the full markdown artifact.

summary: The #380 dev-lock roadmap mirror in build/debug checked out and pushed dev in the main checkout with no adopt-mode fence
description: Introduced by this PR (aa3e45ed, sub-plan 1 Task 7) — NOT pre-existing; the block is absent from dev. The dev-side mirror runs git -C "$REPO_ROOT" checkout dev / commit / push origin dev to mirror the roadmap ledger line onto dev, guarded only by the dev lock. In adopt mode (RUNTIME_WORKTREES=false, WORKTREE_PATH == REPO_ROOT) $REPO_ROOT IS the session sole working tree, so the checkout swaps the branch out from under the in-progress build/debug run, over a tree still holding uncommitted feature work. CUR_BRANCH is restored afterwards so blast radius is bounded, but the fence that exists precisely to refuse this (bkit_close_guard_checkout, which requires RUNTIME_WORKTREES=true AND RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true) was never consulted. Flagged by build-plan-verify-holistic as an untraced risk and carried through the ship deferred sweep without a trace being owed.
rootCause: The close-hook block was written without the runtime double-guard, and the obvious guard could not be dropped in verbatim: bkit_close_guard_checkout installs an EXIT trap, and bash traps REPLACE rather than chain, so it would clobber the DEVLOCK-removal trap and leak the dev lock. Compounding it, RUNTIME_WORKTREES/RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES are set by bkit_runtime_detect in an EARLIER, SEPARATE fenced shell invocation and are not in scope in the close block — so the naive fix (testing those vars inline) would have compared against unset and silently disabled the mirror entirely.
remediation: Added an inline fence at the top of the mirror subshell in both bkit-build.md and bkit-debug.md, before the dev lock is even acquired: if [ "$WT" = "$REPO_ROOT" ] then log and exit 0. Derived from local facts already assigned in the same fenced block rather than out-of-scope RUNTIME_* vars. Faithful proxy for the double guard because the runtime capability table moves both flags together (LOCAL/GITHUB_ACTION/CLOUD_CURSOR => worktrees=true+devpushes=true; CLOUD_CLAUDE/UNKNOWN => both false). Behaviour verified by executing the fence for both modes: adopt skips, mint proceeds. Host mirrors regenerated; bkit check 0 writes.

summary: bkit [auto route] squash-subject marker is never threaded onto dev in a cloud dispatch — the #363 post-merge dev trigger feature is functionally inert
description: bkit-ship.md Step 5 (.bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md:686-704) reads AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX back from a BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE handoff written at Step 1 (:255-262) via `echo "BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE=$BKIT_AUTO_ROUTE_FILE" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`. In a claude-code-action/opencode cloud dispatch every agent Bash tool call executes inside one Action step, so $GITHUB_ENV (which only propagates BETWEEN separate Action steps) never carries the value forward; Step 5 falls back to the dead `echo "${LABELS:-}" | grep -q 'bkit:auto'` read (LABELS unset in that shell), so AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX is always empty. bkit-cloud.yml's free-tier gate (contains(head_commit.message, 'bkit [auto route]')) can therefore never match a dev push, and no dev-CI-failure /bkit-debug dispatch can ever occur — the load-bearing mechanism #363 exists to ship.
rootCause: GitHub Actions $GITHUB_ENV is applied by the runner only between separate workflow steps; it does not propagate across separate Bash tool calls an agent makes within one claude-code-action/opencode run step. A file-path handoff written this way is silently invisible at the point of use in a cloud dispatch.
remediation: Re-derive AUTO_ROUTE_SUFFIX inside the SAME bash fence at Step 5 with a call that depends on no prior shell state (e.g. gh issue view {ISSUE_ID} --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qxF 'bkit:auto'), per docs/knowledge.jsonl key 363-workflow-md-shell-var-does-not-survive-bash-tool-call-boundary idiom (1); delete the $GITHUB_ENV handoff entirely.

summary: maskNonExpansions blanks an arbitrary multi-line span whenever a fenced-block comment contains an apostrophe, because it masks '...' with no awareness of leading # comments
description: .bkit/core/engine/audits/workflows/block-locality-audit.test.ts:160's maskNonExpansions runs out.replace(/'[^']*'/g, blank) over a fenced workflow block with no comment-awareness. A single possessive apostrophe inside a `#` comment (e.g. "script's") pairs with the next literal single-quote anywhere later in the block and blanks every line in between, including real VAR= assignments — the audit then reports a bogus unassigned-$VAR failure pointing at the wrong line. Hit during the #380 round-2 ship remediation (commit 8427ed08): a possessive in a workflow fenced-block comment swallowed a real TRACKER_ROWS= assignment several lines down; worked around by rewording the comment. The defect itself is untouched and will recur for the next author who writes a possessive in any workflow fenced-block comment.
rootCause: Regex-based quote masking (/'[^']*'/g) has no notion of a leading # comment token, so an apostrophe inside a comment is treated as a real quote-open and pairs with an unrelated later quote.
remediation: Not yet fixed — out of #380's scope. Candidate: strip # comment-to-end-of-line spans before running the quote-mask regex, or make the mask comment-aware (skip matches whose opening quote is preceded by an unescaped # earlier on the same line with no closing quote before it).

summary: .bkit/src/bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts bookCommitBlocks selector matches the bare substring bkit-book-commit.sh, so a comment mention counts as an invocation
description: .bkit/src/bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts:79 bookCommitBlocks keeps any bash region containing the substring bkit-book-commit.sh (block.includes at :91), with no distinction between an actual invocation and a comment merely naming the file. A region runs from its opening ```bash to the line before the next ```bash, so a mention in the prose after a block also counts. That inflates the exactly-5-wired-regions assertion at :820 and the every-region-is-guarded assertion at :826 whenever a comment mentions the filename. Hit during the #380 round-2 ship remediation (commit 2b669577) against tests/ship-failure-path.bats, whose awk selector 1cf8ff37 ported to this Vitest file with the same bare-substring match: a comment naming bkit-book-commit.sh broke both assertions; worked around by removing the filename from the comment. The selector itself is unfixed and will recur for the next author who mentions the script by name in a comment near a fenced block.
rootCause: bookCommitBlocks matches on a bare substring rather than a real invocation pattern (e.g. a call site with `.` or `bash` prefix, or a comment-stripped scan).
remediation: The bookCommitBlocks selector and bkit-book-commit.sh no longer exist in .bkit/src/bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts; the book commit is a bkit command. Nothing left to fix.

summary: bkit-ship.md never writes a workflow-started row, so every ship run on an FID folds into one run
description: Build, plan, design and debug each append {type:"workflow-started"} to status.jsonl at start; ship does not (0 occurrences in .bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md). The fold (bkit-status-fold.sh) starts a new run only on workflow-started, so all ship invocations on one FID collapse into a single run. Effects: (1) counter_next/counter_current are active-run scoped, so MERGE_ATTEMPT carries over between separate ship runs — on 380-roadmap-analysis-refresh (4 ship runs, 3 failed) a new ship run would start at MERGE_ATTEMPT 2 of MAX_MERGE_ATTEMPT 3; (2) bkit-ship.md:1399 SHIP_START is always empty, so the outcome row records durationSeconds 0 and frictionAdded/deferralsAdded/failuresAdded count every ship row since epoch instead of this run; (3) bkit-ship.md:1377 COUNTER_VALUE counts workflow-started rows and is always 0.
rootCause: The workflow-started emit (and its resume re-emit) was removed from bkit-ship.md in 80660ac0 (#384, PR #395) restructure; the #384 plan does not mention removing it.
remediation: Restored in bkit-ship.md Step 1 item 8: legacy status.json migration, then workflow-started (with parentSha) unless the latest folded run is ship IN_PROGRESS — same shape as build/plan/design/debug. Guarded by bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts (all five workflows emit it) and bkit-ship-workflow-started.integration.test.ts (runs the extracted fence against the real fold).
